notes:
Summary: Mid-market product org (SaaS B2B) evaluating Redwood. Started with Hosted API to prove integration (chat + embeddings). Now moving to evaluation of Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. Heavy focus on unit economics; will run a technical cost-optimization workshop during POC.

Sales/Deal context (brief):
- AE Maya Chen lead; SE Evan Patel supporting.
- Bought in: Head of Product (Sophie Tran), CTO (Marcus Bell). Procurement loop active.
- Decision drivers: predictable per-instance latency, committed pricing, data residency controls.

Workload profile / requirements:
- Primary: customer support chat for product + doc search (hybrid retrieval with embeddings). Secondary: reranking for in-app recommendations and code-assistant for power users.
- Traffic: peak daytime 350 concurrent sessions; baseline embeddings throughput ~120 qps.
- Latency target: chat p95 < 200ms (interactive flows), embeddings p95 < 400ms acceptable for async indexing.
- Cost sensitivity: high; finance wants modeled unit economics before procurement signoff.
- Models: prefer open/Redwood-verified LLMs; want fallback routing to smaller, cheaper variants under load.

Security/compliance notes:
- Must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance evidence, tenant-level audit logging, KMS integration for key control. Data residency: US and EU regional enforcement required for subsets.

POC / technical milestones (timeline):
- 2024-09-12: initial discovery call (hosted API demo).
- 2024-09-25: Hosted API trial started; integrated chat endpoints in staging (devs: 2 full-stack engineers).
- 2024-10-10: Hosted API performance sanity check; chat p95 ~260ms with default batching (notes: acceptable but not hitting target).
- 2024-10-28: Dedicated demo with SE (Evan) — showed predictable tail latency, autoscaling behavior.
- 2024-11-01: POC statement of work drafted; includes cost-optimization workshop and targeted perf benchmarks.
- 2024-11-06: Security questionnaire in to legal; waiting on vendor risk team for data residency clarifications.

Cost-optimization workshop plan (what we proposed / outcomes expected):
- Topics: batching strategies (session-aware batching), prefix/KV caching proposals, quantization profiles for representative models, and unit-economics modeling per 1M tokens.
- Redwood recommendations from demo: aggressive KV/prefix caching for common prompts -> estimated 20-30% token savings on chat traffic; continuous batching window tuned to 30-50ms to hit p95 targets while improving throughput.
- Quantization: run A/B on q8 and q4-like profiles for embedding and chat models; expectation: int8-like quantization reduces spool GPU utilization and can lower cost ~35-45% for heavy embedding workloads with minimal quality regression. SE to provide sample quant profiles and eval harness.
- Unit economics: compute per-conversation token consumption + cache hit rate; finance asks for three scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic). Redwood asked for 2 weeks of request traces (anonymized) to run a simulation.

Open technical questions / risks:
- P95 under sustained peak with batching tuned — confirming can meet <200ms consistently with dedicated pool sizing.
- Quantization tolerance for code-assistant paths — need eval metrics (exactness/compilation rate) vs baseline.
- Data residency: whether Dedicated region pinning satisfies EU-resident subset requirements or Private deployment needed.

Next steps (short):
- Verdigris to provide 14 days of anonymized request traces and prompt set by 2024-11-12.
- SE Evan to run cost-simulation and produce a 3-scenario unit-economics deck by 2024-11-18.
- Schedule 2-hour cost-optimization workshop (tech + finance): proposed 2024-11-13 10am PT.
- Legal: Redwood to reply to outstanding vendor questionnaire by 2024-11-15.

Rep notes (shorthand, from calls):
- "We like the Hosted API speed to get started but worried about long-term cost."
- "If Dedicated can show 30–40% cost savings with comparable latencies we can move to an MSA."
- Finance: wants committed spend tiers mapped to throughput guarantees.

Attachments / artifacts referenced: pricing deck, POC plan, security FAQ.

Internal Redwood actions:
- SE: set up trace ingestion pipeline; run sim and share quantization A/B results.
- AE: prepare commercial packaging (3 tiers: trial, committed, enterprise) with ARR bands reflecting optimization outcomes.
- Solutions: prepare short live-coding eval harness for code-assistant quant tests.
